parameter_reviews.name: fluid.box_cells

declaration.source: numerical: the fluid box's cell count per side stated outright (cell/assemble.grid_box); 0 = derive the box from fluid.padding. For a series that must place the wall at a chosen distance with a chosen multigrid depth (CALIBRATION-2026-09-20): refused if odd, if not a multiple of fluid.cells_multiple, or if the box does not hold max|x| + fluid.padding, which then acts as a floor

parameter_reviews.finding: Zero means derive the box from positions and padding. A positive declared count is constrained geometrically; it is not a biological cell count.
parameter_reviews.target_context: Frozen MCF7-oriented template; physical solvent references, experimental context, model choices and numerical controls kept distinct. No native execution or source-to-target transfer is verified.

parameter_reviews.name: fluid.cells_multiple

declaration.source: numerical, not biological: cell/assemble.grid_box rounds the fluid box's cell count per side UP to a multiple of this, SYMMETRICALLY. The staggered device grid already rounds to 16 by itself (physics.fluid_mac.MacGrid) but puts the extra cells on the + side only, so the built box is off-centre (row-1 native: 362 asked, 368 built, + walls 0.30 um farther) and is not the box the tables record; 16 here makes the device's rounding a no-op. It buys NO multigrid depth — a first version of this row claimed the native grid had two levels; it has five (368 = 16 x 23), and that claim is withdrawn (2026-09-21). 1 = the box as it always was

parameter_reviews.finding: Symmetric host box rounding is distinct from device MAC rounding with fixed origin. The raw declaration retains stale362/368 commentary; the frozen function itself explicitly withdraws that native attribution.

source_cards.title: IAPWS SR6-08(2011): reference liquid-water density and viscosity correlations
source_cards.access_scope: Full official PDF; §§2–3,6–7 and Tables1,5,8 read; equations transcribed for scalar arithmetic only.
source_cards.primary_anchor: PDF pp.3–4 Eq.2/Table1; p.8 Eq.7/Table5; p.11 Table8

conditions.phase: Stable liquid at the target temperature; source also covers metastable subranges with separate uncertainty qualifications.

source_cards.observational_unit: Temperature/pressure-specific reference correlation; not a cell, cytosol or chamber measurement.
source_cards.finding: Eq.7 gives 0.0006913034204 Pa·s at 310.15 K and 0.0006933287137 at 310 K. Eq.2 gives density 993.3291635 and 993.3830202 kg/m³ respectively. Current 0.000692 viscosity is a close water reference; density 1 pg/µm³ is an approximation, while its g/cm³ unit conversion is exact.
source_cards.limits: The declared CRC edition/table remains unlocated. This IAPWS check is an alternative reference, not proof of that exact citation or a measurement of composite cytoplasm viscosity. Water density is temperature dependent.
source_cards.reported_uncertainty: Source §3.3 gives 1% stable-liquid viscosity uncertainty and §2.3 0.0001% stable-liquid density uncertainty, both expanded with coverage factor k=2; correlation uncertainty is not a cell-population prior.

conditions.examples: ~70% E. coli and D. discoideum; other organisms/tissues differ

source_cards.observational_unit: Whole-cell mass fraction, with organism and assay context; neither cytosolic compartment volume fraction nor free solvent fraction.

source_cards.primary_anchor: Estimation of Membrane Permeability; HTML Table1; Fig.7 and corresponding Results

conditions.volume_estimator: Projected area with spherical geometry assumption

source_cards.observational_unit: Vb/V0 for whole-cell osmotically inactive volume in freezing; not water mass fraction or compartment-resolved water volume.
source_cards.finding: Source Table1 lists V0=2978±127 µm³ and Vb=(0.31±0.02)V0. Complement 0.69 is conditional active-volume fraction in this assay, not direct validation of cytosol water fraction 0.7 at 37 °C.
source_cards.limits: Error type and n for the inactive-fraction estimate are not established by the kinetic-curve n. The historical Teo2013 label is wrong: actual first author is Angela Seawright. Cache names and P17 stay unchanged. No permeability-header normalization is attempted.
source_cards.reported_uncertainty: Keep reported ±0.02 and ±127 with unresolved estimate-specific error type; no SD/SEM or population-prior assignment.

source_cards.title: IUPAC osmotic quantities: activity and ideal particle concentration
source_cards.access_scope: Official search-rendered definitions inspected; direct local HTTP endpoints returned 403 and old host TLS failed. No raw local original byte hash is available.
source_cards.primary_anchor: Gold Book O04344 definition; O04340 osmolality; O04343 osmotic concentration

conditions.scope: incompressible-fluid osmotic equilibrium; ideal dilute-solution reduction
conditions.denominator: Osmolality uses water activity/molar mass; osmotic concentration uses a volume basis.

source_cards.observational_unit: Thermodynamic definition, not a measurement of this medium or cell.
source_cards.finding: The general expression depends on solvent activity. Ideal dilute pressure uses concentration of independently moving molecules and ions, not unqualified nominal salt molarity. Current 300 mM is interpreted by the inspected code as ideal osmolyte equivalents per water volume.
source_cards.limits: The source definitions do not locate the target medium composition, measured osmotic activity or an MCF7 300 mM observation. Osmolality, volume-based osmotic concentration and chemical solute molarity need explicit distinctions.
source_cards.reported_uncertainty: No experimental uncertainty or target distribution.

source_cards.title: NIST revised SI: exact constants and conditional RT conversion
source_cards.access_scope: Official NIST constant definitions; historical source_derivations and chemical-context temperature record re-read.
source_cards.primary_anchor: NIST Meet the Constants, Boltzmann and Avogadro entries

conditions.temperature_role: Declared condition, not a universal constant or observed cell temperature

source_cards.observational_unit: Exact defining constants multiplied by a declared reference condition.
source_cards.finding: R=kB·NA=8.31446261815324 J/(mol·K). At 310 K, RT=2577.4834116275 Pa per mM; 1 mM=1 mol/m³ and 1 Pa=1 pN/µm². Current 2577 is rounded. 310 K and 37 °C=310.15 K are distinct conditions.
source_cards.limits: Not independent numerical evidence from chemical_context/source_derivations; same SI lineage. Actual code pressure uses cell.temperature through kBT; reference_temperature only validates the declared conversion. No empirical variance follows from exact constants.
source_cards.reported_uncertainty: No empirical uncertainty inferred; all prior rows remain unchanged.

source_cards.title: Aquaporin osmotic efficiency: reflection coefficient is solute and channel specific
source_cards.access_scope: Primary cached Methods, Figs2–3 and selected Results re-read.
source_cards.primary_anchor: Methods Water permeability; Fig.2/3; Results Reflection coefficients

conditions.system: Xenopus oocytes with wild-type/mutant AQP1 or AQP9
conditions.observable: Initial 5–10 s volume slope after generally 20 mM osmolyte shifts
conditions.reference: Channel-impermeant reference mannitol for AQP1; sucrose/raffinose protocols for AQP9

source_cards.observational_unit: Same-oocyte test-solute osmotic efficiency σPf relative to impermeant-reference Pf.
source_cards.finding: Near-unity σ for tested wild-type AQP1 solutes is a source-condition result; channel/solute variants differ. The measured efficiency and the reference permeability are distinct quantities.
source_cards.limits: Not MCF7, nuclear-pore transport, or a global sigma=1 measurement. The frozen code permits only ideal impermeant solutes and rejects sigma≠1; that is model scope, not confirmation of native impermeability.
source_cards.reported_uncertainty: Source Methods mean±SEM across oocytes from at least two batches unless noted. No current-row uncertainty/covariance adopted.

source_cards.title: Yasuda et al. 2018: membrane–solvent partial slip theory
source_cards.access_scope: Author preprint v2 HTML equations and discussion inspected; bibliographic journal DOI is linked by arXiv record.

conditions.system: Continuum bilayer plus outer bulk solvent
conditions.quantity: Intermonolayer friction b differs from solvent parallel friction b_parallel and normal permeation resistance b_perp.

source_cards.observational_unit: Theoretical friction coefficients and assumed orders of magnitude, not measured MCF7 slip lengths.
source_cards.finding: Parallel and normal solvent-interface dissipations are separated from intermonolayer friction. The paper estimates b_parallel from water viscosity/molecular size and argues partial-slip effects are small for its ordinary-bilayer parameter regime.
source_cards.limits: Paper symbol b is not the current slip-length b in µm. Code maps positive slip length to two-sided drag 2ηA/b and b=0 to exact tangent constraints. This code mapping is conditional and does not measure zero slip or authorize a new mechanism.

the nuclear envelope is the same bilayer as the plasma membrane; bound to fluid.slip_length_membrane so the two sheets cannot differ by an unstated number. 0 there selects the exact tangent rows on both, which is why osmotic.water_permeation = 1 needs fluid_coupling='saddle'.

the nucleoplasm is an enclosed ~300 mOsm solution too — the statement envelope.volume_modulus's own source row already makes. BOUND to osmotic.internal rather than given its own number: nothing here measures a nucleoplasm/cytosol osmotic offset, and inventing one would put a standing pressure across the envelope at t = 0. Unbind it the moment a measurement exists.
